props.gloss_en: [the Sages] said: one may not insulate, even in a thing that does not add heat, after nightfall
if he comes to add [to the insulation], he adds
how does he do it? RSBG: he takes the sheets and puts the heavy blankets, or takes the heavy blankets and puts the sheets
RSBG: they prohibited [insulating after nightfall] only [in] that same urn
RSBG: but if he poured [the water] from urn to urn, it is permitted
the Gemara: now that he is cooling them, will he boil them?!
[if] he insulated and covered with a thing movable on Shabbat, or insulated in an unmovable thing and covered with a movable one -- he takes [the pot] out and returns it
[if] he insulated and covered with a thing not movable on Shabbat, or insulated in a movable thing and covered with an unmovable one -- if part of it was exposed, he takes out and returns
and if not [exposed], he does not take out and return
R' Yehuda: the chaff of fine flax -- it is like manure
one places an urn on top of an urn
and a pot on top of a pot
but not a pot on top of an urn
nor an urn on top of a pot
and he plasters its mouth with dough
not so that they heat, but so that they be kept [warm]
just as one does not insulate hot food, so one does not insulate cold food
Rabbi permitted insulating cold food
one does not crush snow or hail on Shabbat so that its water flows
but he puts it into a cup or into a dish and need not be concerned
